subject: physics
question_text: A horse has to pull harder during the start of the motion than later. Explain.

verification.note: Sri Chaitanya IPE Junior Fastrack (Rev. May 2024), Unit 5 VERY SHORT ANSWER. The 1+1 mark split is invented and needs a Telangana IPE teacher; no exam appearance years are printed for this question, so appearances[] stays empty.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: At the start
lines: To start the cart, the horse must first
largest value static friction can take.
steps.margin_note: The words worth the mark are "limiting friction". Static friction alone is vaguer.
steps.why: Static friction is not one number. It grows to match whatever pull is applied, up to a maximum — and the cart moves only once the pull passes that maximum.
common_mistakes: Saying the cart is heavier at the start. The mass never changes.

recall.must_convey: That starting the cart means overcoming limiting (maximum static) friction.
accept: maximum static friction has to be crossed
starting lo limiting friction cross cheyyali

steps.memory_tip: Starting must beat MAXIMUM static friction — the largest value friction can take.

steps.label: Once moving
lines: Once the cart is moving, only kinetic
so less effort is needed later.
steps.margin_note: The inequality is the answer. Write it out rather than describing it.
steps.why: While the surfaces slide, the tiny contact welds between them never get time to form fully, so the opposing force drops.
common_mistakes: Writing that friction disappears once the cart moves. It only gets smaller.

recall.must_convey: That kinetic friction is less than limiting friction, so less effort is needed later.
accept: kinetic friction is less than limiting friction

steps.memory_tip: Moving faces only kinetic friction, which is smaller. The order to remember: static maximum > kinetic.

insider_note: The examiner scans for two words, limiting and kinetic. An answer that never names either friction earns one mark at best.
